title: Professional Certificate Course in Understanding Marketing Philosophy and Thought
description: To provide a comprehensive understanding of various marketing philosophies, research methods, and planning frameworks.
longDescription: Understand the influence of culture on consumer behavior with marketing communication as a moderator. Understand the direct influence of marketing communication on consumer behavior. Understand the influence of psychological factors on purchasing decisions. Marketing as a set of tools and business philosophy. The nature of scientific paradigms. Philosophical thoughts such as what do we know? And how do we know? Marketing development as a science and historical context of early science. Theory verification versus theory discovery. Methods bias in marketing research. Suitable paradigm for marketing and the process of scientific marketing research. Understand theory first or data first? Understand marketing thoughts and philosophies such as scientific relativism and scientific realism. Understand the view of reality and marketing research reliance on realism and relativism. Marketing planning conceptual framework. The aim of this short course is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the influence of culture on consumer behavior with marketing communication as a moderator. It also aims to explore various marketing philosophies, research methods, and planning frameworks to enhance participants' marketing skills. After the successful completion of the course, you will be able to learn about the following,
courseDetails: This course provides an in-depth understanding of the influence of culture on consumer behavior with marketing communication as a moderator. You will explore the direct impact of marketing communication on consumer behavior and learn about the psychological factors that influence purchasing decisions. Additionally, you will discover marketing as a set of tools and a business philosophy, and gain an understanding of the nature of scientific paradigms and philosophical thoughts such as "what do we know?" and "how do we know?"
